Maya (infra): seeing gRPC streaming stalls for large model checkpoint pulls between pods in us-west-2a -> us-west-2b, started ~08:12 UTC. apps time out or hang mid-stream.
Evan: which paths? pod->pod or node->node?
Maya (infra): mostly pod->pod across nodes on the same rack, sometimes node->node when kube-proxy routes differ. Impacting some Dedicated GPU jobs — retries spike.
Priya: any packet drops or retransmits in kernel logs?
Maya (infra): yes, kernel shows lots of "IP: packet too big" and PMTU updates. Also saw gRPC error: "stream terminated: CANCELLED (status 1)" in logs.
Sam (eng-runtime): that smells like fragmentation/encap overhead causing packets > MTU and being dropped. Are we on VXLAN overlay with jumbo frames?
Maya (infra): overlay is vxlan on top of 9000 MTU hosts, but I noticed host NIC MTU on some nodes is 1500 (old baremetal reprovisioning).
netops-bot: alert created: NET-4812 - Inconsistent host MTU detected across cluster (count: 6 hosts).
Evan: can you paste ifconfig/ethtool from one bad node + one good node?
Maya (infra): pasted snippet:
```
# node-good
eth0: flags=4163<UP,BROADCAST,RUNNING,MULTICAST>  mtu 9000
  inet 10.1.0.12  netmask 255.255.0.0  broadcast 10.1.255.255
# node-bad
eth0: flags=4163<UP,BROADCAST,RUNNING,MULTICAST>  mtu 1500
  inet 10.1.0.34  netmask 255.255.0.0  broadcast 10.1.255.255
```
Maya (infra): tcpdump showed lots of fragments not reassembling on receiver, and `gso`/`gro` stats were high.
Priya: that mismatch would make VXLAN overhead push inner packets > 1500 and get dropped on host-bad before reassembly, causing gRPC streaming stalls (continuous token streaming fails).
Sam (eng-runtime): we also saw connection stalls on RDMA-capable nodes when a peer was on a node with MTU 1500; RDMA ignores GSO so fragmentation behavior differs.
Evan: temporary mitigation: mark the overlay to ensure smaller inner MTU or force path MTU probing. Try lowering vxlan mtu to 1450 on all nodes or set sysctl `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` and disable GRO/GSO on problematic interfaces for testing.
Maya (infra): ran quick test: `ip link set dev vxlan0 mtu 1450` on one bad node -> gRPC stream recovery immediate.

oncall-robot: scheduled rolling remediation: change host MTU to 9000 where possible else set vxlan mtu across cluster to 1450. Playbook PR: https://git.internal/redwood/playbooks/mtu-remediate
Evan: long term fix: enforce MTU during provisioning + add cluster admission check preventing nodes with MTU < 9000 join Dedicated GPU pools. Also add an e2e test for streaming large blobs (models) under overlay.
Priya: steps I ran for a full rollout test:
- drained 2 nodes in staging
- set eth0 mtu=9000 and rebooted network (systemd-networkd)
- verify `ip link show` and restart kubelet
- run iperf3 + large gRPC stream test with 1M token chunk emulation
Results: no fragments, throughput stable, no gRPC stalls.
Sam (eng-runtime): note for on-prem customers with MTU limits (tenant racks), we should document recommended vxlan MTU formula: host_mtu - encaps_overhead (50-60 bytes) = vxlan inner MTU. Add to docs.
Maya (infra): rolling fix started: patching kube-provisioner to set host MTU and adding preflight check in k8s node bootstrap. Will coordinate with oncall.
Evan: is there a cost/throughput impact for lowering VXLAN MTU (1450 vs 9000)?
Priya: small increase in packets/sec and CPU overhead on encap path, but overall token cost for inference unaffected. For Dedicated GPU workloads it's fine — better than repeated stream retries which killed throughput earlier.
Maya (infra): closing notes: root cause = mixed host MTU due to partial reprovisioning; immediate mitigation = set vxlan mtu to safe value + enable PMTU probing, long term = enforce MTU in provisioning + admission control + doc.
Sam (eng-runtime): nice catch. Please add affected customer list (if any) to NET-4812 and tag CSM.
Maya (infra): added CSM tags, notifying ops and GPU fleet owners. Will follow up with postmortem if any chargebacks/major job failures.
Evan: thanks all, reassigning NET-4812 to Maya for remediation runbook. :thumbsup:
